items.q: Do people who freeze under pressure lack confidence as a trait?
items.a: Usually not. **You don't lack confidence — you struggle to communicate when the situation demands it.** Confidence is how you manage body, prep, and voice.

items.q: Why do hands and voice shake before a presentation?
items.a: Fight-or-flight dumps **excess adrenaline**. Burn it with **20 star jumps** or a brisk **5-minute walk**, then warm the face with lip trills, big/small stretches, and pretend chewing.

items.q: How do you desensitize awkward eye contact in public?
items.a: Play the three-level game: catch eyes → smile "Morning" → look away; then add a compliment; then compliment + question. Aim for about **100 reps**.

items.q: What do you do when sustained eye contact makes your brain panic?
items.a: Use the **triangle technique**: alternate **left eye → right eye → nose bridge** so an anxious brain has a job during contact.
Ask a question that reveals threads, pick one, then ask **three follow-ups** before switching topics. Great conversationalists are curious about the other person.

items.q: Why does your mind go blank at work small talk?
items.a: Often **no prep + default weather/weekend talk**. Craft **five authentic go-to questions** (dreams, free time, mentors, lessons learned) you can reuse.

items.q: How do you get louder without straining your throat?
items.a: **Volume for free**: loud auditory yawns open the soft palate. Babies scream for hours; adults strain because the palate closes. Practice **10–15 yawns daily**.

items.q: How should you show up in a job interview energetically?
items.a: Be the **bringer of vibes** — don't wait for interviewer energy. **20 star jumps**, re-introduce with melody, sustain energy start-to-finish, and open with an informal human question.

items.q: Do credentials beat likability in hiring?
items.a: In business, **we do business with people we like**. A Spotify playlist / Backstreet Boys opener built instant rapport for a Head of Performance hire.
